description: Resources of the Kafka broker pods (cAdvisor, kube-state-metrics, kubelet) and their nodes (node-exporter): CPU incl. throttling, memory vs. limit incl. page cache, disk I/O, network, pressure stall information (PSI) and persistent volume usage with a fill-up forecast.

panels.description: Working set of the fullest broker container relative to its memory limit. Above ~90 % the kernel reclaims page cache aggressively and the OOM killer is close. Kafka needs headroom above the heap for page cache, direct and mapped buffers.
panels.title: Memory vs limit (max pod)

panels.description: CPU used by all selected broker containers.
panels.title: CPU cores used

panels.description: Share of CFS periods in which the broker containers were throttled by their CPU limit. Throttling directly adds latency; > 5 % is noticeable. No data = no CPU limit set (fine).
panels.title: CPU throttled

panels.description: Container restarts of the selected pods during the dashboard time range.
panels.title: Restarts (window)

panels.description: Fullest Kafka data volume (used ÷ capacity from the kubelet). Kafka stops a broker when a log dir is full — act at 80 %.

targets.expr: max((sum by (persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace"}) and on (persistentvolumeclaim) (max by (persistentvolumeclaim) (kube_pod_spec_volumes_persistentvolumeclaims_info{namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"$pod"}))) / (sum by (persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace"}) and on (persistentvolumeclaim) (max by (persistentvolumeclaim) (kube_pod_spec_volumes_persistentvolumeclaims_info{namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"$pod"}))))

panels.title: Volume used (max)

panels.description: Out-of-memory kills of the broker containers in the time range (cAdvisor). Any OOM kill means the memory limit is too small for heap + off-heap + page cache needs.
panels.title: OOM kills (window)

panels.description: CPU cores used per broker container with the container's CPU request (dashed). Usage permanently above the request means the pod competes for CPU with neighbours.
panels.title: CPU usage vs request / limit

panels.description: Share of scheduling periods in which the container hit its CPU limit, per pod. Kafka is latency sensitive: prefer no CPU limit or a generous one.
panels.title: CPU throttling

panels.description: Working set (what the kubelet compares with the limit for eviction/OOM), RSS (JVM heap + off-heap) and page cache per broker. Kafka reads and writes through the page cache: a large cache is GOOD, as long as the working set stays below the limit.
panels.title: Memory: working set, RSS and page cache vs limit

panels.description: Share of time tasks in the container were stalled waiting for memory (pressure stall information, 'some'). Non-zero values mean reclaim is slowing Kafka down even before an OOM.
panels.title: Memory pressure (PSI)

panels.description: Bytes read and written by the broker containers (cAdvisor block I/O). Writes ≈ produced bytes × replication factor; reads > 0 under load means consumers read data that is no longer in the page cache (lagging consumers).
panels.title: Disk throughput per pod

panels.description: Share of time the container's tasks were stalled on I/O. The best indicator of a saturated disk from Kafka's point of view.
panels.title: I/O pressure (PSI)

panels.description: Used bytes of every Kafka data volume and a linear forecast 7 days ahead (predict_linear over 6 h), with the volume capacity. If the forecast crosses the capacity, add disk or reduce retention.
panels.title: Volume usage and forecast

panels.description: Bytes received (up) and transmitted (down) by each broker pod, all interfaces. Includes client, replication and controller traffic.
panels.title: Network throughput per pod

panels.description: Dropped and erroneous packets per pod. Should be 0; drops point to overloaded nodes or CNI problems.
panels.title: Network errors and drops

panels.description: Share of time runnable tasks of the container waited for a CPU. High values with low usage mean the node is overcommitted.
panels.title: CPU pressure (PSI)

panels.description: Non-idle CPU share of the nodes (node-exporter), averaged over cores.
panels.title: Node CPU utilisation

panels.description: Memory available for new allocations on each node (MemAvailable). Page cache counts as available — Kafka benefits from lots of it.
panels.title: Node memory available

panels.description: Share of time each block device was busy (io time). Near 100 % = saturated disk.
panels.title: Node disk utilisation

panels.description: Node-wide pressure stall information: share of time some tasks waited for CPU, memory or I/O.
panels.title: Node pressure (PSI)

panels.description: 1-minute load average divided by the number of cores. Above 1 the node has more runnable tasks than CPUs.
panels.title: Node load per core

title: Kafka · Pods & Nodes
